# Locality Guide: South Windsor, Hartford County, Connecticut (1820–1920)

## Jurisdiction overview
- **Formed:** 1845 from East Windsor
- **County:** Hartford County
- **Prior jurisdiction:** East Windsor (1776–1845); earlier, Windsor (Hartford Colony, 1634–1768)
- **Economy:** Agriculture (Connecticut River Valley tobacco and hay), small manufacturing
- **Religious denominations:** Congregational (dominant; established church until 1818), Methodist, Episcopal, Roman Catholic, Baptist
- **Key note:** Irish Catholic immigration to Hartford County accelerated mid-19th century — Dwyer is an Irish surname; Catholic church records (Diocese of Hartford) may be relevant.

## Boundary changes
- Before 1845: South Windsor was part of East Windsor. All pre-1845 records are filed under East Windsor.
- Before 1776: East Windsor was part of Windsor (later Hartford County).
- Records follow the jurisdiction that created them — search East Windsor for any events before 1845.

## Available record types

### Vital records
- **Civil registration start:** 1866 (state level); generally complied with by 1901.
- **Pre-1850 (Barbour Collection):** Connecticut Vital Records Prior to 1850 — FS collection 2843390; indexed + images. **Primary resource for births/marriages/deaths before civil registration.**
- **1830–1852:** South Windsor Town Clerk vital records (FS catalog 471245) — images, 55% indexed, full-text searchable. FamilySearch Center access may apply.
- **1852–1910:** South Windsor Registrar of Vital Statistics (FS catalog 471248) — images, ~46–48% indexed, full-text searchable.
- **1897+:** Connecticut State Library marriage/death indexes; Ancestry and Reclaim the Records marriage index 1897–2017.
- **Death records and parents:** Pre-1905 death records do NOT name parents. From 1905, parent names may appear but informant accuracy varies.

### Church records
- **Congregational (dominant):** South Windsor church records 1694–1898 (FS vol. 008141255, browse-only images); baptism/marriage registers 1829–1936 (FS vols. 008200169, 007951347 — full-text searchable). Methodist, Episcopal church records also exist.
- **Catholic (Diocese of Hartford):** Given the Irish-surname context, Catholic baptism and marriage registers are high priority. Connecticut Church Records 1660–1955 (FS collection 2658799, indexed); CT Church Record Abstracts 1630–1920 at Ancestry.
- **Repository:** Connecticut State Library holds many deposited church records.

### Census records
- **Federal census:** 1820–1940; all years indexed + images on FamilySearch/Ancestry. 1850 South Windsor census volume is 98% searchable.
- **Relationship to head listed from 1880.** Check all census years to build household profile and identify co-resident family members.

### Probate records
- **Probate district:** Hartford (covers South Windsor).
- **FamilySearch digitized volumes** (full-text searchable, 0% name-indexed): 1813–1922, covering South Windsor and East Windsor jointly for earlier volumes.
- **Ancestry:** Connecticut Wills and Probate Records 1609–1999 — indexed + images.
- **Probate files (original papers):** FS catalog 141959 (1787–1880, browse-only); FS catalog 606675 (1881–1915, browse-only).
- Probate records (wills, administrations, guardianships) are an excellent source for naming children and establishing family relationships.

### Land records
- Connecticut is a state-land state. Deeds recorded at town level (South Windsor Town Clerk).
- Colonial Land Records 1640–1846 (FS catalog 84462) — images.
- Land records can place individuals in time and associate them with neighbors/kin.

### Cemetery records
- **Hale Collection** (FS collection 2658554, 1640–1955): indexed burial records and obituary abstracts — high-value resource.
- Find a Grave: South Windsor cemeteries listed.
- Hartford County Cemeteries on FamilySearch Places.

### Newspapers / obituaries
- Connecticut Hale Collection includes newspaper notices 1629–1934 (FS collection 2658554).
- Ancestry Newspapers.com index covers Connecticut papers.
- Obituaries post-1905 may name parents and siblings.

### Military records
- Civil War (1861–1865): draft registrations, service records.
- Connecticut Military Census Questionnaires 1917 (FS collection 3741249, indexed + images).
- WWI/WWII draft cards on Ancestry/FamilySearch.

## Repository guide

| Repository | Key holdings | Access |
|---|---|---|
| FamilySearch | South Windsor vital records 1830–1910; probate 1813–1922; CT Barbour Collection; church records; census | Free (some center-only) |
| Ancestry | CT Wills & Probate 1609–1999; Barbour Collection; marriage/death indexes; census | Subscription |
| Connecticut State Library | Original vital records; church record deposits; court records | In-person / online index |
| South Windsor Town Clerk | Original vital records, land records, town meeting minutes | In-person / mail |
| Diocese of Hartford Archives | Catholic baptism, marriage, burial registers | Contact archives |

## Records NOT online
- Original South Windsor land/deed records (pre-digitization) at Town Clerk
- Some Catholic parish registers (Diocese of Hartford archives)
- Some church records not yet deposited at CT State Library

## Research tips
- **Start with the Barbour Collection** for any pre-1850 vital event; then move to the FS town vital record volumes for 1830–1910.
- **Pre-1845 events:** Always search under East Windsor, not South Windsor.
- **Parentage from death records only possible 1905+.** For earlier parentage, use church baptism records, probate (naming children in wills), and census household reconstruction.
- **Irish Catholic context:** The surname Dwyer suggests Irish origin; Catholic church registers and naturalization records are worth checking alongside civil vital records.
- **Probate full-text search:** FS probate volumes are full-text searchable — use FamilySearch full-text search with the subject's name to locate will or administration references.
